title: How Many Ways Does a Graph Look the Same?

concept.title: Map the vertices one by one and check the edges to the vertices already mapped
body: An *automorphism* of a graph is a way to rename its vertices (a permutation `p`) so that the graph looks exactly the same: there is an edge between `u` and `v` **if and only if** there is an edge between `p(u)` and `p(v)`. The identity is always one. A square has 8 automorphisms (4 rotations and 4 reflections); a complete graph on `n` vertices has `n!`. We want their number.

Decide the images of the vertices in the order 0, 1, 2, ... For vertex `i` try every vertex `t` that is not yet an image. Check the new pair against **every vertex already decided**: `adj[i][j]` must be equal to `adj[t][image[j]]` for all `j < i`. A vertex can only map to a vertex of the **same degree**, which is an even earlier test.

The consistency check works because every edge and every non-edge is checked exactly when its second end gets an image. The count is a plain number of leaves of this tree: up to `n!` = 40320 for 8 vertices (no edges or all edges), and very few for graphs with little symmetry.

statement: A graph has `n` vertices and `m` edges. Count the permutations `p` of the vertices such that for every pair of vertices `u` and `v`, there is an edge between `u` and `v` exactly when there is an edge between `p(u)` and `p(v)`.
inputFormat: Each of the next `m` lines has two vertices joined by an edge.
outputFormat: Print the number of such permutations.
constraints: 0 <= m <= n * (n - 1) / 2, no repeated edges and no loops

examples.note: A square has 8 symmetries: 4 rotations and 4 reflections.

hints: Map the vertices in order; a vertex can only go to an unused vertex of the same degree.
For the new pair check the edge between the vertex and every earlier vertex against the edge between their images.
Count one when all vertices are mapped.

n, m = map(int, input().split())
edges = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(m)]

explanation: Images are chosen vertex by vertex among unused vertices of equal degree; a choice must agree with the edge or non-edge to every earlier vertex and its image. A complete mapping is one automorphism.
solution.complexity: Time up to O(n! * n) (40 320 leaves for n = 8), space O(n).
